downstream.relationship: Largest hyperscaler customer; purchases massive volumes of H100/H200/B200 GPUs for Azure AI cloud infrastructure and OpenAI partnership

downstream.name: Tesla Inc.

NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI accelerator value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, critically dependent on TSMC for advanced-node manufacturing and SK Hynix for HBM memory while commanding extraordinary pricing power over hyperscaler and enterprise downstream customers who have few viable alternatives for high-performance GPU compute. Its position as the de facto standard for AI training workloads gives it exceptional leverage across both directions of the supply chain, though concentration risk is elevated on both the TSMC manufacturing side and among a handful of mega-cap cloud customers that together represent the majority of Data Center segment revenue.

upstream.name: Qualcomm Inc.
upstream.relationship: Supplier of 5G modem chipsets (Snapdragon X-series) used in iPhones pending Apple's in-house modem transition

upstream.name: Broadcom Inc.
upstream.relationship: Supplier of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and RF/networking chips integrated across iPhone, iPad, and Mac product lines

upstream.name: Micron Technology
upstream.relationship: Supplier of DRAM and NAND flash memory used in iPhone, Mac, and iPad devices

upstream.name: Honeywell International
upstream.relationship: Supplier of specialty materials, sensors, and industrial components used in device manufacturing and data center operations

downstream.name: Microsoft Corporation

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a complex global supply chain, acting primarily as a fabless designer that outsources manufacturing to a concentrated set of Asian semiconductor and display suppliers — most critically TSMC for its proprietary silicon — while distributing finished products through a mix of direct retail, carrier partnerships, and third-party resellers worldwide. Its downstream is uniquely diversified across hardware product lines and a fast-growing Services segment, reducing customer concentration risk, though its dependence on Google's search licensing agreement and a handful of major carriers for iPhone distribution represents meaningful revenue dependencies.

upstream.name: ASML Holding N.V.
upstream.relationship: Critical supplier of EUV and DUV lithography equipment essential for advanced DRAM and NAND manufacturing

upstream.name: Applied Materials Inc.
upstream.relationship: Major supplier of wafer fabrication equipment including CVD, PVD, and etch systems for memory production

upstream.name: Lam Research Corporation

downstream.name: Amazon.com Inc.

downstream.name: Alphabet Inc.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the core of the global memory semiconductor value chain, sourcing highly specialized fabrication equipment from a concentrated group of equipment makers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) to manufacture DRAM and NAND at scale. Its products are essential inputs for hyperscalers, AI accelerator vendors, and consumer electronics OEMs, with demand increasingly driven by AI workloads requiring High-Bandwidth Memory and high-capacity enterprise SSDs.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM occupies a uniquely asset-light but strategically pivotal position in the semiconductor supply chain, sitting upstream of virtually the entire chip industry by licensing CPU, GPU, and system IP rather than manufacturing silicon itself. Its primary dependencies are on EDA software vendors like Cadence and Synopsys for design tooling, while its downstream customer base spans nearly every major fabless chipmaker, OEM, and hyperscaler — making royalty and licensing revenue highly diversified yet deeply tied to global chip demand cycles.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company occupying a critical middle position in the data infrastructure supply chain, relying heavily on TSMC for advanced node fabrication and ARM for processor IP while designing custom and merchant silicon for hyperscalers, networking OEMs, and storage customers. The company has strategically pivoted toward AI-driven custom ASIC co-development with major cloud providers (Amazon, Google, Microsoft), making hyperscaler demand the dominant driver of its revenue trajectory.
